look_here_first: With a flowering sample, turn over ONE capitulum. FNA: a long slender CYLINDRICAL involucre 8–10 mm with overlapping phyllaries in 4–6(–8) series, rather than the short hemispheric 2–3-series involucres of Conoclinium. Leaves are opposite, generally 3-veined and coarsely toothed with elongated deltate-lanceolate outline; shoots are tall and sometimes sprawling/clambering. Do NOT rely on purple/white color.

morphology_keys.growth_form: Perennial to subshrub, typically 80–250 cm, erect, spreading or subscandent, stems hispidulous/pilose.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; petioles generally 5–20 mm, blades narrowly lanceolate to deltate-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, typically 3–10 × 1–4 cm; coarsely toothed to nearly entire; 3-nerved.
morphology_keys.heads: 5–50+ small discoid capitula in terminal or lateral corymbiform arrays; no ray florets.
morphology_keys.involucres: CYLINDRICAL 8–10 mm long, phyllaries in 4–6(–8) series with inner tips appressed and rounded to truncate.
morphology_keys.florets: Purplish, light blue, white or pinkish tubular disk florets; color variable and not reliable alone.
morphology_keys.fruit: One-seeded cypselae bearing a pappus of bristles, important to photograph but not yet locally matched against look-alikes.
morphology_keys.bloom: Mostly Oct–Dec in FNA US treatment, may flower longer in subtropical areas.
morphology_keys.habitats_fna: Hammocks, thickets, pinelands, disturbed sites; US FNA 0–30 m (coastal pattern; not evidence for Central Texas nativity).

priority_matrix.separate_by: Cylindrical individual involucre 8–10 mm, 4–6+ phyllary series versus short hemispheric heads with 2–3 series; leaf outlines can both be triangular and toothed.
C. dissectum leaf margin deeply cut/dissected, and small hemispheric heads; fragrant mistflower generally has simple toothed blades and elongated cylindrical heads.
Both can be shrubby with opposite toothed leaves: measure one individual involucre, Chromolaena 8–10 mm vs Ageratina 4–6 mm; inspect head shape and phyllary series, not only flower color.
White snakeroot is herbaceous rhizomatous with broad long-petioled leaves; Chromolaena often subshrubby with notably longer cylindrical involucres.
Late boneset usually a tall herb with white clustered heads; inspect an individual head's involucre, leaf attachment, and persistent woody framework.
